interfaces.name: targets
interfaces.type_desc: TensorFlow float32 Tensor or convertible float32 array
interfaces.constraints: Finite nonempty shape (N,1), aligned row-for-row with predictions. Explicit float32 required; no automatic float64 conversion. Caller supplies target units, row identity and observation availability.

interfaces.name: predictions
interfaces.type_desc: TensorFlow float32 Tensor or Variable or convertible float32 array
interfaces.constraints: Finite shape (N,Q) for pinball or (N,3) for clipped score. Same units as targets. Pinball columns align with quantiles; score columns are low, point, high. Crossing is permitted. Tensor/Variable conversion preserves the TensorFlow gradient path when used within the caller gradient tape.

interfaces.name: minimum_scale
interfaces.constraints: Positive finite Python scalar, excluding bool, remaining finite and positive in float32. Floor on high-minus-low spread, in target units. Crossed or negative spreads encounter this floor.

interfaces.name: maximum_error
interfaces.constraints: Positive finite Python scalar, excluding bool, remaining finite and positive in float32. Cap on absolute point error, in target units. No unit conversion is performed.

interfaces.name: result
interfaces.constraints: Scalar float32 Tensor: row mean of sqrt(2)*min(abs(target-point),cap)/max(high-low,floor) + log(sqrt(2)*max(high-low,floor)). Numeric score depends on the caller unit convention; the logarithm uses the numerical scale in those units. Piecewise differentiable, with TensorFlow subgradients at boundaries. No calibration guarantee. Concrete provisioned TensorFlow execution only; abstract witness rejects. No training, optimizer or state mutation. Extreme finite float32 inputs can overflow intermediate arithmetic; callers must check loss and gradients before updates. TensorFlow tensors and gradient tapes are in-process objects; JSON/HTTP serialization is not qualified.

limitations: Automated Tier 3 for concrete provisioned TensorFlow execution only; no human Tier 1 or empirical Tier 2 claim.
Caller establishes target units, row identity, column alignment and observation availability; no domain policy is inferred.
Pinball carries target units. The clipped score logarithm depends on the numerical unit convention; scores from different unit conventions cannot be compared directly.
Crossed predictions are permitted. Neither objective establishes calibrated uncertainty or ordered quantiles.
GradientTape must enclose the call; JSON transport, remote execution and abstract simulation do not preserve this qualified differentiable interface.
Finite float32 inputs may overflow intermediate arithmetic. Callers must check loss and gradients before optimizer updates.
Synthetic analytic tests and source comparisons qualify numerical behavior, not empirical transfer or the full OSIC workflow.
Installed RECORD integrity and dependency constraints do not authenticate publishers or qualify clean-platform installation or redistribution.
